skill.name: claude-reflect
skill.description: Capture Claude Code corrections locally and review them before turning reusable feedback into project or global instruction files.
skill.summary: Turn reviewed Claude Code feedback into durable team instructions.
skill.author: BayramAnnakov

security_audit.summary: Static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown references to Claude paths, slash commands, repository URLs, and bounded cache-removal instructions. The skill has a medium privacy concern because it automatically retains correction text and can scan local session history; proposed writes require human review.

remediation.issue: Automatic collection and retention of correction text and session history
remediation.suggestion: Document the local data stores, add an opt-out for automatic capture and history scans, and provide a clear command to review and delete queued data.

remediation.issue: Potentially sensitive content can be proposed as persistent instructions
remediation.suggestion: Redact likely secrets before queueing and show the exact destination and diff before every approved write.

semantic_findings.title: Automatic Retention of Feedback and Session History
semantic_findings.description: The skill automatically queues correction text and can scan past Claude Code sessions. This can retain sensitive user-provided content in local Claude data stores before the user reviews proposed memory changes.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documentation explicitly states that hooks queue corrections automatically and that historical scans examine past sessions. Human review protects writes, but does not prevent local collection and retention of sensitive text.

content.user_title: Capture and apply Claude Code learnings
content.value_statement: Repeated corrections can be lost between Claude Code sessions. Claude Reflect collects reusable feedback locally and lets you review it before updating instruction files.
actual_capabilities: Detects common correction phrases and explicit remember markers during Claude Code sessions.
Queues detected feedback locally for later review.
Lets you preview queued learnings with /view-queue and discard them with /skip-reflect.
Uses /reflect to review, edit, skip, and apply reusable learnings to instruction files.
Scans past local sessions for missed corrections when you request /reflect --scan-history.
Suggests reusable skill candidates from repeated session patterns with /reflect-skills.
limitations: Automatic capture can retain sensitive correction text in local Claude data stores.
Human review is required to apply learnings, so the process is not fully automatic.
Pattern detection can miss feedback or queue text that is not a reusable instruction.
Historical scanning depends on local Claude Code session data that is still available.

use_cases.title: Maintain project conventions
use_cases.description: Review repeated corrections and save approved coding conventions in a project instruction file.

use_cases.title: Preserve personal preferences
use_cases.description: Store reviewed preferences in a personal local instruction file without changing shared project guidance.

use_cases.title: Find reusable workflows
use_cases.description: Analyze repeated requests and review suggested Claude Code skills for recurring work.

prompt_templates.title: Review queued feedback
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: inspect captured learnings before making changes.

prompt_templates.title: Apply one reviewed learning
prompt_templates.prompt:
/reflect
Review the queued learnings. Apply only reusable project conventions to this project.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: convert reviewed feedback into project guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Preview history scan
prompt_templates.prompt:
/reflect --scan-history --dry-run
Show candidate learnings from available past sessions. Do not write any files.

prompt_templates.title: Discover workflow skills
prompt_templates.prompt:
/reflect-skills --days 30 --dry-run
Find repeated workflows from the last 30 days. Explain the evidence and propose no files.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: identify skill opportunities before generation.

output_examples.input: Run /reflect after several corrections about testing.
output: A review list of queued corrections
A proposed reusable instruction about running tests
A prompt to choose a destination before writing
Candidate learnings from available local sessions
A preview without generated skill files

best_practices: Inspect queued learnings before applying them to any instruction file.
Keep project conventions in project files and personal preferences in local files.
Use dry-run mode before historical scans or skill discovery.
anti_patterns: Do not approve queued text that contains secrets, credentials, or private personal data.
Do not apply broad global instructions when a project-specific rule is sufficient.
Do not treat every correction as a durable convention without reviewing its context.

faq.question: What does Claude Reflect capture?
faq.answer: It detects common correction phrases and explicit remember markers, then queues the related feedback locally.

faq.question: Does it write instruction files automatically?
faq.answer: No. You review proposed learnings through /reflect before applying them.

faq.question: Can I inspect or remove queued items?
faq.answer: Yes. Use /view-queue to inspect pending items and /skip-reflect to discard them.

faq.question: Can it scan previous sessions?
faq.answer: Yes. Use /reflect --scan-history to find missed corrections in available local session history.

faq.question: Where can approved learnings be saved?
faq.answer: The skill can propose global, project, local, rule, and skill instruction destinations.

faq.question: How should I handle sensitive feedback?
faq.answer: Review the queue carefully, remove sensitive text, and avoid storing secrets in instruction files.
